scope: Independent mathematical and primary-source audit for the small matrix-completion comparison; does not certify the manuscript proofs or empirical competitiveness.

shcgm.title: Stochastic Frank-Wolfe for Composite Convex Minimization
shcgm.assumptions: Bounded variance and strong duality; Theorem 2, page 4

problem.observations: Omega is a fixed set of N distinct observed matrix entries; y_ij fixed, finite.
problem.smooth_gradient_lipschitz_constant: 1/N in Frobenius norm, assuming distinct observed entries
problem.LMO: -tau*u_1*v_1^T for a largest singular-vector pair of H; zero is a valid choice if H=0
problem.relative_interior: 0 belongs to int(C) intersect int(D); Slater condition and both relative-interior requirements hold.
problem.boundedness: f is globally smooth and convex, C compact, and f and component gradients are bounded on C.
problem.repair_proof: Scaling by a factor in (0,1] preserves the nuclear-norm ball and enforces every box bound. Elementwise clipping by itself need not preserve the nuclear-norm constraint.
problem.linear_regularity: For X in C, dist(X,C intersect D)<=||X-R(X)||_F<=max(1,tau)*dist(X,D). If maxabs(X)=a>1, ||X-R(X)||_F=||X||_F*(a-1)/a<=tau*(a-1)<=tau*dist(X,D).

oracle.draw: Fresh iid uniform index I=(i,j) from Omega, independent of the past conditional on current X.
oracle.variance_bound: E||G_I-grad f||_F^2 <= (tau+max_Omega |y_ij|)^2 for X in C.
oracle.minibatch: Average B independent draws with replacement; mean unchanged and conditional variance divided by B.
oracle.duplicate_indices: A minibatch may contain repeats; accumulate repeated coordinate gradients, then divide by B. Never overwrite duplicates.
oracle.oracle_count: After k updates: B*k sampled entries and k minibatch calls, since the first sampled gradient is reused for update 1. Diagnostics are counted separately.

sframes.indexing: k=0,1,... indexes current X_k before update k+1.
sframes.initialization: Initialize smooth-gradient momentum from the first minibatch at X_0; do not multiply that first minibatch by rho0.
sframes.paper_exact_schedule_case: gamma0=rho0=1 is the literal displayed prescription in Proposition 2.11; beta0 is free positive.
sframes.tuned_prefactor_scope: User expressly permits tuning fixed positive prefactors with theoretical exponents fixed. Label these runs fixed-exponent prefactor tuning, rather than claiming the displayed theorem literally specifies every tuned constant.
sframes.rate: O(t^(-1/4)) for the averaged true smoothed FW gap, with p=3/4,q=1/4,r=1/2.
sframes.other_claim_scope: Original-gap and feasibility statements (66)-(67) concern a subsequence selected through expected gaps; they are not an arbitrary last-iterate rate.
sframes.manuscript_sign_discrepancy: Algorithm 1 line 6 in the supplied draft prints Proj_D(Tx)-Tx, opposite to the derivative of its positive squared-distance penalty. Use +(X-clip(X))/beta as explicitly defined in the objective and Section 2 analysis, consistently with prior experiments.

shcgm.indexing: Paper k=1,2,...; an implementation zero-based update j uses k=j+1.
shcgm.tuning_scope: Keep eta and rho formulas including offsets/constants exactly as in Algorithm 1. beta0 is a free positive input and may be selected with a disclosed grid.
shcgm.assumption_result: Convex smooth f, compact C, closed convex D, finite variance, and strong duality all hold for this test.
shcgm.rate_scope: Theorem 2 controls expected objective residual and feasibility; no finite-run optimizer ranking follows.
shcgm.reproduction_scope: This is an implementation of the published SHCGM algorithm on a new synthetic problem. It is not an exact reproduction of published MovieLens losses, train/test split, dimensions, or objective scaling.

metrics.theorem_average: If reporting the SFRAMES theorem statistic, sum true gaps at every pre-update iterate X_0,...,X_(t-1) using each current beta. Sparse checkpoint averages, stochastic-direction gaps and best-so-far gaps are not substitutes.
metrics.raw_objective: f(X) at an infeasible X can lie below the constrained optimum. Do not label it a feasible optimality gap.
metrics.feasible_objective: Evaluate f(R(X)), with the disclosed radial repair above, and save repair distance. Repair is diagnostic and never feeds the update.
metrics.reference_dual_lower_bound: For arbitrary Xr and Z, LB=f(Xr)-<grad f(Xr),Xr>-tau*||grad f(Xr)+Z||_op-||Z||_1 <= f_star. For a convex reference solver use Z=box_upper_dual-box_lower_dual.
metrics.reference_proof: Convexity lower-bounds f by its tangent; min_(X in C)<grad f(Xr)+Z,X>=-tau||grad f(Xr)+Z||_op, and sup_(X in D)<Z,X>=||Z||_1.
metrics.reference_accuracy: Compare an independently evaluated feasible upper bound f(R(Xr)) to the dual lower bound. Report the resulting interval rather than assuming solver status alone proves accuracy.
metrics.timing: Separate optimizer time from diagnostics, feasible repairs, exact-gap SVDs, reference solve and plots. Also retain total wall time. Initialization and tuning scope must be stated.
metrics.target_time: Compare the first measured time to shared feasible-loss/feasibility targets, not endpoints after one method has already plateaued.

fairness: Same fixed instance, same initial matrix, FP64, batch sizes and iid index streams per seed across methods.
Different trajectories imply different gradient values even when sampled coordinate indices coincide.
Use disjoint tuning and confirmation seeds; freeze configuration selection before inspecting confirmation results.
Do not equate identical nominal beta0 with identical initial smoothing: SHCGM starts beta0/3 and SFRAMES starts beta0.
Use exact SVD-based LMOs at the small scale; an approximate leading singular-vector solve requires its own error control and theory mapping.
A convex test is covered by the nonconvex SFRAMES theory but does not demonstrate a nonconvex advantage.
SHCGM exploits convexity and has a stronger convex guarantee; no SFRAMES win should be presumed.
validation_suggestions: Finite-difference the full smooth gradient and positive squared-box-distance penalty at interior, exterior and boundary matrices.
Enumerate every observed-entry gradient on a tiny instance and compare its exact average against the full gradient.
Use a repeated-index minibatch to detect assignment-versus-accumulation bugs.
Validate LMO feasibility and its objective against -tau*largest_singular_value on generic and rank-deficient gradients.
Verify prescribed schedule values at first and several later updates, including the SHCGM offsets and zero-momentum initialization.
Check nuclear-norm invariance of every FW update and both constraints after radial repair.
Audit the reference primal-dual interval independently from the chosen convex solver.
Verify that identical seed/batch settings generate identical entry-index streams for both methods without reading diagnostic RNG draws.
Cross-check the accumulated true-gap sum against independently recomputed saved tiny-run iterates to catch off-by-one errors.
